# Link Alloy 0.0.2 — connection distribution and diagnostics alpha

Download **Link Alloy Portable.exe**, save it in a writable folder, and run as administrator. No ZIP extraction or installer is required. Settings includes the bundled license and all third-party notices. The verified Wintun runtime is embedded and extracted beside the EXE when needed. WebView2 must be available on Windows.

## Changes

- Application/service cohorts distribute new TCP connections across eligible adapters using atomic weighted rotation. Unrelated upload traffic no longer drives all new download connections toward the apparently idle adapter.
- Process attribution uses Windows TCP ownership tables, including IPv4 and IPv6. Unknown ownership safely falls back to service-level distribution.
- Connections now shows application/PID, connection ID, assigned link, actual upstream local address, connection time, live rates, and transferred bytes. Completed diagnostics have bounded retention. Endpoint and process details remain in memory; event logs correlate start/end using flow IDs.
- Regression tests cover concurrent bursts across two, three, and four links, configured weights, normal monitor refreshes, dial fallback, disabled links, process ownership, and bounded diagnostics.
- Direct portable EXE release with SHA-256 checksums; notices are included inside the executable.

## Test this version

1. Pause the download, stop the previous tunnel, and close the old Link Alloy process.
2. Launch this EXE as administrator, enable the intended links, and use equal weights for the first comparison.
3. Start the tunnel, reopen the launcher, and resume the download.
4. Open Connections and filter for `steam.exe` (or your launcher). Compare actual received bytes on each adapter over sustained overlapping windows.

This alpha targets connection placement and makes it measurable. The new real Steam/EA/Epic comparison remains pending user testing. It does not split one existing TLS/TCP connection, include a CDN optimizer, or provide relay-based packet bonding. A speed increase is not guaranteed. ICMP and fragmented packets remain unsupported. Stop the tunnel before exiting.

The portable application is unsigned. Windows signing and the remaining physical link-loss/crash-recovery validation are still stable-release gates. The explicitly permitted unsigned alpha tags are v0.0.1 and v0.0.2; later release gates remain enforced.
